title: Approximation Algorithms for Size-Constrained Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization in Deterministic Linear Time

problem.claim: Maximize a non-negative submodular function subject to a limit on the number of selected items.

gap.claim: Prior work did not provide deterministic, linear-time approximation algorithms for the non-monotone version of this problem.

contributions.claim: A single-pass streaming algorithm with approximation ratio 23.313 + ε.
A simpler deterministic linear-time algorithm with approximation ratio 11.657.
A deterministic (4 + O(ε))-approximation algorithm and a deterministic e + ε-ratio algorithm running in O_ε(n log(n)) time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The streaming algorithm has approximation ratio 23.313 + ε.
The simpler deterministic linear-time algorithm has approximation ratio 11.657, and another algorithm has ratio 4 + O(ε).
The O_ε(n log(n))-time algorithm achieves ratio e + ε, described as close to the best known expected ratio e - 0.121 in polynomial time.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines cardinality-constrained maximization of a non-negative non-monotone submodular function and notes application relevance.
Claims the first deterministic linear-time approximation algorithms without assuming monotonicity.
Lists three deterministic linear-time algorithms with streaming and approximation-ratio guarantees.
Adds an e + ε-ratio deterministic algorithm with O_ε(n log(n)) runtime and compares it with a reported expected ratio.

source_observation.claim: The work combines deterministic guarantees, linear or near-linear runtime, and multiple algorithmic forms including streaming.

interpretation.claim: For cardinality-constrained non-monotone optimization, runtime model and determinism can be treated as explicit design objectives alongside approximation quality.

application.claim: When designing similar selection algorithms, evaluate streaming compatibility, determinism, approximation ratio, and runtime together.

exception.claim: The reported guarantees are stated for non-negative submodular objectives under a cardinality limit and may not transfer to other objective classes or constraints.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithms' assumptions beyond non-negativity, submodularity, non-monotonicity, and a cardinality limit.
The abstract does not provide experimental results, datasets, proof details, memory bounds, or independent verification.
